https://lifi.uber.space/cockpit.title: Team Cockpit
https://lifi.uber.space/cockpit.description: Your link, live: what your LED sends and what your sensor measures, on one shared timeline. If the two do not match, you are looking at your bug.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: the photo digitiser
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: turn an analog photo into numbers: pick resolution and colour depth (down to the game boy's four greys), see the picture change, and watch the byte count grow.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: the audio digitiser
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: the same two cuts for sound: choose sampling rate and bit depth, see the staircase on the wave — and hear what gets thrown away.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: the copier
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: press copy and hang each generation on the wall: watch the analog picture fade copy by copy, then ask what a file would have done.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: pixel painter
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: an 8×8 picture, one bit per pixel: paint and watch the bytes write themselves, edit the hex and paint with numbers, then break a byte and see the damage.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: inside a file
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: a real bitmap in a hex editor: header fields underlined, click a pixel to find its three bytes, then change a byte — and watch the picture obey, or the viewer refuse.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: byte switchboard
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: flip eight bits and watch the number appear: binary, decimal, hex, and the ascii character behind it.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: drift simulator
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: two clocks, slightly apart: watch the receiver’s sampling points wander out of the time slots until the message turns to garbage, then let a sync marker save it.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: distinguishability lab
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: send symbols over a noisy channel, oscilloscope style: grow the alphabet, tune the window, inject a disturbance, and watch the error rate fight the throughput.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: question game
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: find the secret face among sixteen: every answer shrinks the crowd, the shrinking is measured in bits, and the halving strategy shows why four questions are enough.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: the pixel filter
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: make a photo brighter one addition at a time: step through a single pixel with its bits and carries, then let the machine do the other sixteen thousand in a blink, and see what happens at 255.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: the gate lab
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: switches in, lamps out: flip the inputs of a single gate, watch a half adder carry, chain eight full adders into a byte adder, and make two gates remember a bit.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: the ipo test lab
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: change sensor values and the classification rule, compare actual with expected output, and watch the test pass or fail.

https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.title: the noisy sensor
https://winf-hsos.github.io/lifi-concept.description: One reading is a draw. A series reveals the distribution.
